---
title: Execution records
---

## Overview

When Quarto runs the code in a document, it can keep what the code produced
--- each cell's outputs and each inline expression's value --- as an
**execution record**. A record lets Quarto present the document again
without running anything: `q2 preview` and hub use
this to show an up-to-date page while you edit prose.

A record is an ordinary Jupyter notebook file (`.ipynb`), whichever engine ran
the code, so other tools can read it. Each cell of the notebook is one
**unit** of the document: a code cell, or an inline expression.

::: callout-note
## Opt-in for now

A plain `q2 render` writes no record. You ask for one per document with
`record: true`, shown below. The preview and hub write records of their own
behind the environment variable `QUARTO_ENGINE_RECORD_WRITE`, which is off by
default while the feature is rolled out; set it to `1` to turn them on.
:::

## Writing a record

Add `record: true` to the document's `execute` options:

````markdown
---
title: Report
jupyter: python3
execute:
  record: true
---
````

A render then writes the record under the project's `.quarto/` directory, at
`.quarto/execution-records/<document path without extension>.ipynb`. In a
project, `reports/q3.qmd` gets `.quarto/execution-records/reports/q3.ipynb`
at the project root. A standalone document with no project gets a `.quarto/`
beside it, so `q3.qmd` gets `.quarto/execution-records/q3.ipynb`.

Two renders of the same inputs write the same bytes. Many projects ignore
`.quarto/` in version control, so a record is not something to commit; do not
expect it to be shared between collaborators until a durable use for it
exists.

## What an edit does to a record

Quarto compares a record with the document to decide whether it still
describes it:

| You edit                                             | The record is |
|------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| prose outside cells and spans                        | still fresh   |
| the code in a cell                                   | stale         |
| a `#|` option line                                   | stale         |
| an inline expression                                 | stale         |
| a front matter key that affects execution            | stale         |

So correcting a typo in a paragraph does not re-run your cells in the preview
or in hub. Any other edit above does.

The preview also keeps a cache of its own, keyed on the whole input. A prose
edit can therefore still cause a re-run there for reasons unrelated to the
record; the table is about the record only.

## Positron's cache is a different file

[Positron](https://positron.posit.co) keeps its own cache of Quarto outputs,
in per-user storage. Quarto does not use or write that file as its record,
for three reasons: Positron's file is rewritten from a fixed set of fields, so
extra information in it is dropped; it is named after a hash of the document's
location, which Quarto cannot reproduce; and it carries a timestamp that
changes on every write, so its bytes are never stable.

Quarto does not read Positron's cache when it renders. The two files stay
independent: neither one reuses the other's outputs, and a render never changes
or deletes Positron's cache.

## Limits

- A record from the knitr engine can be stored, but Positron cannot present
  rendered knitr output yet.
- To run cells in a kernel other than Python, see
  [Running other languages with Jupyter kernels](jupyter-kernels.qmd), which
  also covers choosing a kernel and what happens when one is missing.
- Inline expressions are described in
  [Inline expressions](computations.qmd#inline-expressions).
